newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen expects $1 billion soft loans from IMF, EU.
newsitem.headline: Yemen expects $1 billion soft loans from IMF, EU.

text.p: A Yemeni official on Tuesday said his country expected the 15-nation European Union and other donors meeting in Brussels this week to extend $1 billion worth of soft loans to the impoverished Arab state.

"We have reached an agreement in principle with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund on steps aimed at boosting economic reforms," Finance Ministry undersecretary Ahmad Ghalib Ahmad said.
"Under the terms of this agreement, the IMF, the World Bank and donor nations would extend $1 billion in soft loans to Yemen to help implement economic reforms," he said.
Ahmad said Yemen's Minister of Planning and Development Abdul-Qader Bagammal left for Brussels on Saturday to attend the two-day meeting scheduled to start on Wednesday.

Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest states, is implementing a stringent three-phase economic reform programme prescribed by the World Bank and the IMF to rid the country of a mounting budget deficit, high unemployment and soaring inflation.
